advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `contradicts` so it only references a surviving (kept) finding, or document that it may point to a co-dropped finding in overlapping-pair cases.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py:151: `keep = pair["b"] if idx == pair["a"] else pair["a"]`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py:152: `drop_map[idx] = combined[keep].get("id")`
'contradicts': drop_map[i] is emitted at line 162 with no guarantee that drop_map[i] refers to a surviving finding
ABSENCE: no test exercises two overlapping contradictory pairs where both members are dropped, so the dangling-reference case is unverified
advisory.finding: apply_contradiction_drops can set a dropped finding's `contradicts` field to the id of a finding that is ITSELF dropped by another overlapping pair. `keep` is selected (line 151-152) without checking whether `keep` is already in, or will later enter, drop_map, so with two cross-referencing contradictory pairs the recorded `contradicts` audit pointer references a finding that no longer survives in blocking/advisory.
scenarios: A verdict with ≥3 findings where the model emits pairs (0,1 drop 0) and (1,2 drop 2): finding 2's contradicts points to id of finding 1, which is also dropped.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the cross-checks are intended to fire on initial reviews (not only re-reviews) and align the ADR/comment framing, or add a re-review gate to match the drift floor.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/drift_floor.py:300: `if not (drift and drift.get("eligible")):` — the drift floor self-gates to the re-review regime
xcheck.maybe_apply_contradiction only checks `contradiction_xcheck_active` + `len(combined) < 2`; no re-review/regime gate
docs/adr/0052...md: 'Re-running review-plan on an unchanged, previously-signed plan ... MUST yield a verdict with no NEW blocking findings' frames the mechanism as re-review-scoped
advisory.finding: The two cross-checks run on EVERY review when their config flag is active, not gated to the stale-head re-review regime that the analogous drift floor requires (drift.get('eligible')). The ADR and config comments frame these as a 're-review-stability' convergence mechanism for 'an unchanged, previously-signed plan re-reviewed at a drifted HEAD', but maybe_apply_contradiction / maybe_apply_comment_trail apply the drops on an initial/signing review too.
scenarios: A first-ever plan review with the flag enabled drops a contradiction or comment-trail-resolved finding, altering the signing verdict rather than only converging a re-review.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that injects a runner whose run() raises and asserts the verdict is left byte-identical (no drops) for both maybe_apply_contradiction and maybe_apply_comment_trail.
evidence: xcheck.py:215-217 `except Exception: ... logger.warning("contradiction sub-call failed..."); return []`
xcheck.py:354-356 `except Exception: ... return {}`
ADR 0052: 'Every drop is fail-safe toward KEEP: ... a failed sub-call ... drops nothing.'

The only active-path tests (test_maybe_apply_contradiction_runs_subcall_when_active, test_maybe_apply_comment_trail_runs_subcall_when_active) supply a well-formed FakeRunner(structured=...); no test supplies a raising runner.
advisory.finding: The fail-safe 'sub-call failure → drop nothing' contract (the module's central resilience claim, per ADR 0052) is untested: no test injects a runner whose run() raises, so the `except Exception → []/{}` paths in `_assess_contradictions` and `_assess_comment_trail` are never exercised.
scenarios: A runner or structured-validation error at review time when the xcheck flag is enabled
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests using a fake runner whose run() raises, asserting v['dropped'] == [] and the verdict string is unchanged for each maybe_apply_* entry.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test exercising _assess_comment_trail's reshape: non-dict item skipped, non-int/out-of-range index dropped, and later duplicate-index item winning.
evidence: xcheck.py:357-364 filters `if not isinstance(item, dict): continue` and `if isinstance(idx, int) and 0 <= idx < len(findings): by_index[idx] = item`
Docstring xcheck.py:324-325: 'a non-int / out-of-range index is dropped; a later item wins.'

test_plan_review_xcheck.py only calls apply_comment_trail_drops with a hand-built resolved_map and the active sub-call test supplies a single well-formed assessment; no test drives _assess_comment_trail with malformed/out-of-range/duplicate items.
advisory.finding: The `_assess_comment_trail` reshape logic (skip non-dict items, drop non-int / out-of-range `index`, 'later item wins' for a duplicate index) is untested, despite being deterministic behavior on realistic malformed model output.
scenarios: Model returns an assessment with a string index, an index past the finding count, a duplicate index, or a non-object entry
advisory.suggested_fix: Feed a FakeRunner whose assessments include a non-dict entry, an out-of-range index, a non-int index, and two entries with the same index, then assert the resulting resolved_map keeps only in-range int indices with the later item winning.
